newsitem.title: INDIA: Doctors optimistic Mother Teresa will recover.
newsitem.headline: Doctors optimistic Mother Teresa will recover.

text.p: Doctors treating Mother Teresa said on Tuesday they were optimistic she would recover soon.
"She is fine," Dr D.P. Shetty, head of the medical panel treating the Roman Catholic nun at a heart clinic in the eastern city of Calcutta, told Reuters.
"I am hopeful that she will recover very soon," he added.
Shetty said Mother Teresa sat up in a chair and said her prayers soon after she woke up. Then she took morning tea. "She had a good sleep and she is much better than on Sunday."
Mother Teresa, 86, had surgery to clear two blocked arteries last week, but spent a weekend battling a long-standing lung problem and poor kidneys. She also had pneumonia.
She is revered as a living saint for her work with the poor, the homeless and the terminally ill.
On Sunday, clinic officials said doctors were concerned that the problems would delay her recovery.
But on Monday, they were more optimistic.
"She is stable and we are very optimistic about her recovery," U.S. doctor Patricia Aubanel, a member of the team treating Mother Teresa at B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre, said.
Dozens of nuns at the headquarters of her Missionaries of Charity religious order attended mass in the "Mother House", as it is called, early on Tuesday. They prayed for over an hour.
"Please pray for our Holy Father (Pope John Paul) and our dearest mother's speedy recovery," read a message on a blackboard outside the chapel.
